nodes.label: The Method 1.6 (main volume)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One claim, demonstrated on one object, with every place the demonstration failed reported; the register is offered as proof rather than apology.

nodes.label: The Lach Cylinder
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The title names a closed index of transitions and the languages they speak; §13.1 defends the ordering and §13.2 insists the cells are transitions, not states.

nodes.label: Lambda — the closed index of atomic transitions
nodes.rationale: Λ is deliberately a recoding that adds no physics, so whatever it exhibits is a property of indexing rather than of atoms.

nodes.label: Closed index
nodes.rationale: Closure gives exactly six things — alphabet, bounds, totality of the membership test, admissible cells, adjoinable axes, imposable constraints — and three further mechanisms are available but are not consequences of closure.

nodes.label: The closure operator R (ℛ)
nodes.rationale: Extensive, monotone, idempotent — 150 of 150 on all three axioms; it reconstructs value sets and pairwise monotone bounds from an index's own extension.

nodes.label: Closure defect E(X) = |R(X)| − |X|
nodes.rationale: Openness is a measurement and closure is the case where the measurement is zero; the book claims no novelty for the machinery, only for computing the closure defect of an index.

nodes.label: The periodic table's defect of 36 cells
nodes.rationale: The table's own coordinates (period, group) admit 36 cells that do not exist: you have to be told period 1 holds two elements, the table cannot tell you. Λ's external definition cost over the same 118 elements is zero.

nodes.label: Transition cell (n, l, k, q, e, f, g, 2S)
The seven constraints and their four origins
nodes.rationale: Exhaustiveness matters because it is the reason the object's properties can be attributed to indexing rather than to physics smuggled in through a bound; every constraint has the single form x_i <= phi(x_j).

nodes.label: The constraint graph is a tree (treewidth 1)
Pauli exclusion as a constraint origin
Distributive, modular, Sperner — and not symmetric
The single expression F
nodes.rationale: A closed expression exists at all (§11.7) because the coordinates couple only along a tree; F(1) = 976 and F(−1) = 2 at the caps of §7.4, and F(−1) = 2 has a cause rather than being a coincidence.

nodes.label: The seventeen generators
The void
nodes.rationale: The void is the shadow of the exclusion principle: void-free fraction 27.7–30.1% across 776 million pairs, stable with no trend, and the seven constraints are correlated by a factor of 1.49 above independence because they descend from two origins.

nodes.label: The Möbius function of Lambda in closed form
The occupancy measure and the arithmetic encoding
nodes.rationale: Two classical functions appear as lattice quantities, and log of the occupancy measure is an ordinary l-1 metric — which is what converts the additive form of slack into the multiplicative one.

nodes.label: The cylinder over the transfer
nodes.rationale: A cylinder and not a Möbius band, 'over nu' and not 'graded by nu'; the cylinder is a fibration whose fibres are two-body, and it does not factorise and then it does.

nodes.label: The tower — Lambda-9 to Lambda-13
nodes.rationale: Five further coordinates (2S', v, 2J_c, K, 2J) extend Λ8 to Λ13 when target spin, seniority and angular-momentum coupling are carried explicitly; the order is fixed as J_c, then K, then J.

nodes.label: The clock in the constraint — Lambda-9's directed composition
nodes.rationale: The clock is an assumption and the assumption can be removed; an index has a time column exactly when its cells are moves.

nodes.label: The dichotomy — counting coordinates close exactly, coupling coordinates close as envelopes
nodes.rationale: Three forms are excluded — a sum, a difference, a symmetric function — and §12.11.2 proves the exclusion is forced rather than observed; 2S <= k is an envelope at 48.5% density.

nodes.label: Self-reference — alphabet, order, bounds (S1, S2, S3)
nodes.rationale: S2, the order, is the hard one: what works above d = 2 is propagation along the tree, and so Λ contains its own order.

nodes.label: Self-defence — the counting argument D = dim q − rank dPhi/dp >= 1
nodes.rationale: Verified on seven dimension pairs and 420 random nonlinear maps; no closure required and no smoothness beyond differentiability. A closed index contains its own contradiction.

nodes.label: The D_phys / D_def split
nodes.rationale: The split came from refusing the conclusion that w = V·e 'detects nothing': a relation that cannot be violated by data is not empty, it is defending the derivation. Tested under four unrelated perturbations with identical verdicts, so the split is not an artefact of which law one varies.

nodes.label: D3 — totality catches a missing value
The six disjoint defences, three of them not runnable by the book
nodes.rationale: The first four compare the book against the book; a conflation is an agreement between the book and itself about a word doing different work elsewhere, so D_ref, D_dict and D_gro reach a coordinate the book does not carry — what a term refers to.

nodes.label: Extension — E1 cells, E2 axes, E3 constraints
nodes.rationale: E is derived rather than posited (§17.5); a set cut out by a sum bound is not closed, which is why no constraint in Λ is a sum or a difference.

nodes.label: The law of realised closure
nodes.rationale: An open index closes only where a certificate exhibits an operation on the coordinate system reaching a fixed point; where a certificate exists E measures the drawing, where none exists E measures the world.

nodes.label: E(X) is the prediction budget
nodes.rationale: An index may be complete or predictive and not both, because a prediction is a proposal about an unlisted cell and completeness is the property of having none. Not a limitation discovered late — it is what completeness means.

nodes.label: nu is inadmissible as an axis
Retrieval as a lattice problem, and rho
nodes.rationale: A paywall blocks a source and not a cell; the secondary can be better than the primary; rho is a property of (document, route) and the chapter collapsed the second index.

nodes.label: A language is a coordinate system (P20)
nodes.rationale: The language a question is posed in bounds whether it can close and at what cost. The selection rules written as a congruence give E = 750; written as E1/M1/E2/M2 the same law is monotone and E = 0 — the notation was the coordinate that made the rule expressible.

nodes.label: The documentary language, which has no closure mechanism
nodes.rationale: 'Has anyone said this before?' carries no algorithm, which is why the precedent question can be bounded and never settled.

nodes.label: The cypher analysis
nodes.rationale: It was not designed, it was noticed and then made explicit: ask each language in turn whether it can speak of the object and read the answer off the pattern of who answers and who does not. The singleton criterion is §33.4.

nodes.label: Translation, and what it costs
nodes.rationale: One object, two namings, and E is the price; E = 0 is relative to coordinates and the coordinates must be given. The certificate is a translation, exhibited and checked.

nodes.label: The bracket
nodes.rationale: It uses only measured neighbours, fits nothing, assumes no functional form and returns an interval rather than a value — a deduction and not a prediction: a fit says where a level probably is, the bracket says where it cannot fail to be. It is limit-free, and §22.4 computes the price of limit-freedom.

nodes.label: The trivial bracket, and the 789-cell disclosure
nodes.rationale: The defect bracket passes 546 of 789 while the trivial form E(n−1) <= E(n) <= E(n+1) passes 789 of 789 because a Rydberg series rises monotonically by construction — so 100% is a signature rather than a proof. Four numbers for one collection is stated as a disclosure, not a reconciliation (registers 783, 797).

nodes.label: The cost surface V = 4nu/3
nodes.rationale: V is a bound and not a tool; it is a function of nu/h alone, which makes depth and step interchangeable. The floor 32/11 = 2.909 is algebraic before it is physical and owes nothing to atomic physics.

nodes.label: The cost is the Newton decrement
nodes.rationale: The cost has a name in another field, and §23.8.4 states the attribution the book owes.

nodes.label: The term function is self-concordant
nodes.rationale: Self-concordance is what explains the cancellation that makes V depend on nu/h alone.

nodes.label: The collection
nodes.rationale: Two collections and only one of them is bracket-tested; the census of §24.12 is computed rather than searched, and the gaps are structural exclusions rather than omissions.

nodes.label: Four ways a species declines
The failure condition, and its inversion
The bound in the silence
nodes.rationale: A method that has never failed has not been tested; the collection never enters the failure regime, and what looks like a prediction is a deduction from measured neighbours offered as falsifiable. 1,061 perturbation bounds came out of a bracket's non-failure.

nodes.label: Collective sections, and the assembly rule
nodes.rationale: Error amplifies as the exponent, which is the point; one dimension, fifteen perspectives, and the bracket is the wrong tool here.

nodes.label: Slack — one quantity under three measures
nodes.rationale: E(X) is the slack counted, the void is the slack counted over an interval, V is the slack measured; all three compare admitted against actual and differ only in whether the comparison is a difference or a ratio. The three languages agree because the three objects are one shape.

nodes.label: Slack is a description length
The Register of withdrawals
nodes.rationale: 1,635 entries over three populations — defects found by auditing, decisions revised, errors made while computing. What the register is evidence of is not that the work was error-prone but that the errors were converted into structure. The proportion caught by instrument rose 5% to 25% while the proportion caught by hand fell 88% to 55%.

nodes.label: Redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.rationale: The object, the protocols, the audits and the collaborator each catch a class the others cannot, and they were not looking at the same thing. The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16 is the worked case: the bracket held 56 of 56 and could not notice because Z cancels from containment.

nodes.label: A dependent choice is indexable
Two registers, and only one of them is a backlog
Precedent, and what a search can bound
nodes.rationale: Novelty is not the author's to claim; what can be claimed instead is a bound on a search. Nine results were derived from scratch that were already in print, and the protocol that should have prevented it said 'enumerate before searching' where it should have said 'search before deriving'.

nodes.label: The reorderability law
nodes.rationale: Reorderability is a constraint system whose arity is the number of axes on which two cells differ; at arity <= 3 the language is entirely bijunctive and the problem is linear, at arity >= 4 it contains 1-in-3-SAT and admits no Schaefer class. The procedure is the law read at low arity and the hardness the same law read at high arity.

nodes.label: Reorderability correctly identified as lattice embedding
nodes.rationale: R-closure and closure under join and meet are the same condition — 1,487 instances, zero disagreements, confirmed on all 475,800 pairs of Λ — so the question is lattice embedding and not an interval problem; a draft's withdrawal of Stahl & Wille and Yannakakis is itself withdrawn.

nodes.label: The interval machinery — C1P, monotone endpoints, PQ-trees
The method outside spectroscopy
String theory — three objects on the pole
nodes.rationale: The partition function is Λ's expression with counts where F has booleans; both close for dual reasons — the string's modes are independent, Λ's coordinates couple only along a tree. Capped coordinates give a finite index and a Sperner bound, so there is no Hagedorn point and no critical dimension.

nodes.label: The Calabi–Yau catalogue, and 540 predictions
nodes.rationale: Self-duality measured, the thin tip read as a defect of the construction rather than of the object, and the Pareto strength taken against the right denominator.

nodes.label: The law applied to this book
nodes.rationale: A work asserting that complete indices are self-referencing and self-defending has no standing if it is not one; the book's cells are (claim, location, support) and its coordinates are part, chapter and section. §32.4.1 says why the recursion is safe — logic without negation.

nodes.label: The Löwdin challenge
nodes.rationale: Löwdin asked for the n+l rule, but the rule is not what atoms obey — deriving n+l exactly would mean deriving something false at two elements, so the target is the ORDER and n+l is a name for it that is 89% accurate.

nodes.label: The occupation law nu(n, l, q)
nodes.rationale: Both Pauli quantities appear: the capacity 2(2l+1) governs admissibility and sits inside the radicand, which is the count of states below. Occupancy enters only through Pauli — raw occupancy makes every scatter figure worse — so the law needs no new coordinate.

nodes.label: Madelung's rule inverts 5d/4f and 6d/5f
nodes.rationale: Lanthanum opens 5d at Z = 57 and actinium opens 6d at Z = 89; seventeen of nineteen openings agree and two do not.

nodes.label: The Löwdin solution — the chained walk
nodes.rationale: One number goes in (c = 137.035999); at each Z the self-consistent field of the ion carrying Z−1's configuration is converged, every frontier channel solved in that frozen field, and the deepest channel is the entrant. The carried state Chapter 34 proved necessary is carried by the equation itself.

nodes.label: Three bodies, and what a complete index is allowed to say
nodes.rationale: The challenge was to ask whether three negatives together ARE the solution: the stratification of M_{E,L} is an index, it closes at E = 0, and therefore predicts nothing — which is Brudno's theorem on the chaotic stratum. 'Completely solvable as a stratification' and 'no trajectory formula exists' are one statement.

nodes.label: Mass-uniformity
nodes.rationale: Every mass-dependent quantity enters through c_ij and the three collision rays; the manifold, metric, norm polynomial and constraint graph are mass-free, so a change of masses cannot create a sixth fixed point, close a meet or open a join.

nodes.label: The twenty-two prime audits
nodes.rationale: Ten test the index and twelve test the book; the twelve protect the reader from the author. Audits exist because an audit that reads the wrong artefact will pass anything — 107 blank boxes across 44 pages while every audit reported clean, because all of them read the source and none read the page.

nodes.label: The principles P1–P23
nodes.rationale: Principles say what an index is and ten admit exact mathematical statement; P10, P12 and P18 are unassigned.

nodes.label: The protocols
nodes.rationale: Protocols say how to work with an index; they are procedural and none is a theorem. They were written by the author and violated by the author in the same week, which is why the object and the collaborator are not optional.

nodes.label: §2.14 — state the number before the interpretation
nodes.rationale: It exists because the failure was measured rather than deplored: conclusions written before reading the output, with the contradicting numbers on the same printed line. It happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so no amount of care fixes it.

nodes.label: §2.16 — the grid, the book's method stated
nodes.rationale: It is the method and not a technique, and it classifies the whole of Q; a reduced question is still open.

nodes.label: §2.17 — triangulation: three results locate a fourth
nodes.rationale: It is a check as well as a method, which is why it belongs with the protocols rather than the principles.

nodes.label: §2.24 — never one heuristic
nodes.rationale: §2.8's two independent routes does not by itself forbid running a single heuristic; §2.24 names the one thing it does not say.

nodes.label: §2.20 — the prime directive: nothing runs unbounded
The seed of Lambda — the closure of seven cells
nodes.rationale: The seed is constructible and is a size rather than a set; it is linear in dimension and the coefficient was in the bibliography. A stable core of four exists and is NOT necessary, and the completions are a heavy-tailed redundancy rather than a tie.

nodes.label: Appendix E — Q, an index of tractable ignorance
nodes.rationale: Q had been recomputed six times with each recomputation written beside its predecessor, so the appendix carried three live item counts. An index states its current contents once and its history as history — ten open of 14, E(Q) = 0 fibred by domain.

nodes.label: Appendix F — the numbers, indexed
nodes.rationale: The appendix first took the wrong domain — the book's own printed figures — because an account of a volume's printed figures belongs to the making of the volume, not to what the volume is about. The construction survived the change of domain; the readings did not. Six kinds of quantity, each fibred over an ordered ground.

nodes.label: Appendix G — Transitions v3.0, indexed
nodes.rationale: Transitions v3.0 is the source of thirty-seven objects and was an address no reader could follow; the thirty sections the book rests on are set out with what rests on each. The eight Register citations are left exactly as written because register entry bodies are never edited.

nodes.label: The Method 1.6 — Spectra Compendium, Part II
COORDINATES-2.13 (104,832 cells)
Bergman's Double-projection Theorem
Baker and Pixley (1975)
Montanari 1974, Networks of constraints
Dechter 1992, From local to global consistency
Freuder 1982 — the corrected mis-citation
nodes.rationale: Freuder gives backtrack-free search under strong (w+1)-consistency, not global consistency; the book had been citing it for Dechter's theorem, corrected at register 400.

nodes.label: Deville, Barták and Van Hentenryck 1999 — staircase constraints
van Beek and Dechter 1995/1997 — row-convexity and constraint tightness
nodes.rationale: The tight-pair count is exactly twice the book's envelope-step number S; the tightness half of the entry went unused for four cycles.

nodes.label: Dilworth 1950 — order dimension of a finite distributive lattice
Rival 1973/74 — lattice embedding and irreducible intervals
Larson 1998
Siggers 2016 — Lemma 3.5(ii) states phi_ij exactly
Booth and Lueker — linear PQ-tree construction
Edlén 1964, examined at one remove
nodes.rationale: Every equation in the review is a fit and the paradigm is stated twice explicitly; one near miss, and it is not ours.

nodes.label: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12)
Cowan and Andrew 1965 — the four pure coupling types
Löwdin 1969 — the filling-rule challenge
Saari 1971, 1973 — collision set of measure zero
Xia 1992 — non-collision singularities at n = 5
Brudno's theorem on the chaotic stratum
Montgomery's shape map as the closure certificate
Aitken's Delta-squared has an exact bias on a Rydberg series
Muon-Catalysed Fusion (Lach 2026) — a singleton admissible set
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The same bracket machinery applied to a parameter rather than a measured value returns an admissible set with one element — a use the book had not stated.

hyperedges.label: The three consequences of closure (self-reference, self-defence, extension)
Slack — E, the void and V as one quantity in three languages
The Löwdin challenge closed — order, law, walk
